content: I have just finished formalizing in Lean/mathlib the model category structure on simplicial sets, which is Quillen equivalent to the model category structure on topological spaces I obtained earlier this year.

The formalization (about 42k lines of code https://github.com/joelriou/topcat-model-category) includes:

  • the theory of anodyne extensions following Sean Moss, Another approach to the Kan-Quillen model structure, https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.04887
  • the fundamental groupoid and the homotopy groups of Kan complexes;
  • the homotopy sequence of a fibration;
  • the theory of minimal fibrations;
  • (cartesian closed) categories of convenient topological spaces: in particular, we obtain a topological realization functor which commutes with finite limits from the category of simplicial sets to the category of Delta-generated spaces

The most technical part of the proof was showing that if p : E ⟶ B is a fibration of simplicial sets, then the map |E| ⟶ |B| on the topological realizations is a Serre fibration. Using an argument by Quillen, we may assume p is a minimal fibration (case initially proven by Gabriel and Zisman), and also that B is a connected finite simplicial set. An induction on the number of simplices of B allows to show that |E| ⟶ |B| is a "topological bundle" (locally on the base, it is a product with |F| where F is a fibre of p, at least if we work in the category of Delta-generated spaces).

In order to deduce that |E| ⟶ |B| is a Serre fibration, one needs to know that the property of being a Serre fibration is local on the base. For this Gabriel and Zisman sketched a "small cubes" argument; instead, I have used the barycentric subdivision, and doing so, I have made an essential use of results by Sean Moss which gave a combinatorial description of (strong) anodyne extensions.

After polishing the code, my intent is to add essentially all of this to mathlib so as to allow more developments of homotopy theory and (co)homology theories in Lean. (Throughout this year, I have made about 80 PRs to mathlib that are related to this project.)
Discussion topic: #maths > The model category structure on topological spaces
